Description:
LLM & Prompt Engineering
* Foundations of Large Language Models (LLMs): 
Introduce the core concepts, capabilities, and limitations of LLMs, including how they process and generate text.
* Programmatic Usage of LLMs: 
Demonstrate how to integrate LLMs into applications using Python. Showcase best practices for handling multiple or repetitive requests (e.g., batch processing).
* Prompt Engineering Techniques: 
Explore fundamental frameworks for designing prompts, including the use of Python triple-quoted strings and f-string formatting to dynamically incorporate context.
Learning Outcome:
* Discover the use cases of LLM solutions.
* Apply foundational prompt engineering techniques to improve model performance and handle repetitive or sequential tasks.
* Learn and build prompt templates in Python using triple quotes and f-strings for flexible and maintainable code.
Project Timeline:
Project Briefing
* Capstone Assignment: 
Building an Interactive LLM-Powered Solution

- Category A (Sensitive) or B (Non-sensitive)
- Group of 2 to 4
- Develop a web-based application that addresses a problem statement from your agency or enhances citizen interaction with publicly available information related to a specific government process or transaction.

This project aims to showcase the ability to design and develop a user-friendly web application that serves as a platform for citizens to efficiently access and navigate essential government-related information.

Description:
LLMs and the Parameters
* LLM Parameter Overview: 
Provide an in-depth look at core LLM parameters
- tokens, temperature, top-k, top-p and other parameters.
* Structured Data in Prompts: 
Illustrate how to incorporate structured data (e.g., CSV, HTML tables) into prompts for more precise outputs.
* Quality & Safety Measures: 
Address potential pitfalls such as prompt injections, content moderation (self-harm, unlawful, or hateful content), and output validation.
Learning Outcome:
* Learn and apply the important parameters such as temperature, top-k, and top-p impact the style, diversity, and accuracy of LLM responses.
* Discover the major LLMs and aware of different LLMs’ capabilities, performance trade-offs.
* Learn to embed and parse structured data in prompts for tasks such as data cleaning, analysis, or reporting.

Scope: Building System with Advanced Prompting & Chaining
Description:
Use Case Archetypes #1: Building Systems with Advanced Prompting and Prompt Chaining
* Advanced Prompting: 
Dive into instruction-based prompting techniques that enhance the model’s reasoning and output quality.
* ChatCompletion API & Chat History: 
Explore the ChatCompletion API for multi-turn conversations, maintaining and leveraging conversation history effectively.
* Multi-Action & Prompt Chaining: 
Examine how to chain multiple prompts (e.g., Sequential Chains, Router Chains) to solve complex, multi-step tasks.
* Quality & Safety Measures: 
Address potential pitfalls such as prompt injections, content moderation (self-harm, unlawful, or hateful content), and output validation.
Learning Outcome:
* Develop multi-step LLM pipelines to tackle intricate problems.
* Implement advanced prompting techniques to guide the LLM’s reasoning process, improving relevance and accuracy.
* Evaluate and filter LLM inputs/outputs to ensure safety, reliability, and compliance with ethical guidelines.
* Apply sequential and router chains to orchestrate multiple LLM calls in a single workflow.
Project Timeline:
* Ideation & Project Proposal Submission with group members: 
Guide participants through the process of conceptualizing an AI solution, defining its scope, and proposing a feasible plan. This includes identifying the core problem statement, target users, and the specific use cases the solution will address.

Description:
Use Case Archetypes #2: From Embeddings to Applications
* Embeddings Fundamentals: 
Explain how embeddings represent text in high-dimensional vector spaces and why they’re crucial for semantic understanding.
* Use Case #1: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG): 
Show how RAG can combine LLM generation with external knowledge sources for more accurate and up-to-date outputs.
* Use Case #2: Search & Retrieval Beyond Keywords: 
Demonstrate how embedding-based search can outperform traditional keyword searches in tasks like recommendation or classification.
* Use Case #3: Predictive Analytics: 
Explore how embeddings can be leveraged for predictive tasks (e.g., clustering, similarity scoring) in data science pipelines.
Learning Outcome:
* Learn and apply the underlying mechanisms behind embeddings
* Learn to incorporate external data retrieval into LLM workflows, improving factual accuracy and context.
* Apply embedding-based methods for semantic search and retrieval, enabling more nuanced data exploration.
* Learn to build embeddings feed into predictive analytics, fueling tasks such as sentiment analysis, anomaly detection, or recommendation engines.

Description:
Use Case Archetypes #3: Chat with Your Data – A Deeper Dive into RAG
* Pre-Retrieval Optimization: 
Investigate strategies for preprocessing and organizing data to improve retrieval quality and speed.
* Enhanced Retrieval Techniques: 
Discuss best practices for indexing, vector databases, and similarity scoring to find the most relevant context.
* Post-Retrieval Processing & RAG Evaluation: 
Cover techniques for refining retrieved information (e.g., summarization, ranking) and evaluating overall RAG performance.
* Proprietary Data & Access Control: 
Address how to securely integrate private data into RAG pipelines while maintaining granular control over usage.
Learning Outcome:
* Build and refine a retrieval-augmented pipeline capable of handling proprietary or domain-specific data.
* Learn and apply the mechanisms that unpinning the performance of a RAG applications
* Learn to build an LLM solution with ability take in proprietary data and info, with granular control on the how these data/info being used in the pipeline.

Description:
Use Case Archetypes #4: LLM Agents with Tools
* Agents & Multi-Agent Systems: 
Introduce the concept of autonomous LLM “agents” that can decide how and when to use external tools or APIs.
* Function Calling & Tool Integration: 
Show how to enable LLMs to call functions (e.g., calculators, web search, or APIs) to complete tasks requiring external capabilities.
* Development Environment Essentials: 
Provide an overview of Python development setups using VS Code, virtual environments (venv), and package management with pip.
* Python for App Building: 
Cover best practices for writing and running Python scripts, including exception handling and debugging.
Learning Outcome:
* Learn to create LLM solutions that dynamically select and invoke tools to gather real-time information or perform the given tasks.
* Learn to build LLM solutions that can gather and use latest information from the Internet or other sources.

Description:
Building AI Apps (Part #1)
* Streamlit Basics: 
Introduce Streamlit’s architecture, focusing on quick, user-friendly interfaces for AI pipelines.
* Linear Execution & Multi-Page Apps: 
Demonstrate how to create straightforward input-output flows, then expand into multi-page designs for better user experience.
* Local Deployment: 
Show how to run a Streamlit app on a local machine for rapid prototyping and testing.
* Project Proposal Refinement: 
Guide participants in refining their initial project ideas, focusing on feasible scope and clear objectives.
Learning Outcome:
* Learn to build a simple web application that serves the LLM pipelines to the users
* Learn to build LLM solutions that can take in dynamic inputs from the users or existing data or files
* [Project] Refine Project Proposal #1

Scope: Beefing up and Deploying the Prototype
Description:
Building AI Apps (Part #2)
* Advanced Streamlit Features: 
Delve into state management, form handling, callback functions, and other advanced capabilities that enable complex application flows.
* Project Structure & Best Practices: 
Discuss how to organize a Streamlit project for scalability, including folder structure, environment files, and modular code organization.
* Streamlit Cloud Deployment: 
Demonstrate secure deployment options, including password protection, to allow external users to test the application.
* Containerization (Optional): 
Introduce Docker basics, showing how to containerize a Streamlit app for consistent, portable deployment across different environments.
Learning Outcome:
* Learn to deploy a web-based app to allow others to access and use
* Learn to package the LLM POCs/MVPs into containerized image that has great compatibility with * various environments
* Experience the deployment process on CStack which can be used by WOG officers without direct access to GCC

Description:
Capstone Session
* Core Processes as Python Scripts: 
Walk participants through implementing the core logic of their proof-of-concept (PoC) in Python. Focus on the functional pieces (e.g., data retrieval, embeddings, prompt engineering) and how these components fit together in a larger pipeline.
* Dynamic Inputs & Interactivity: 
Illustrate how to integrate dynamic inputs (e.g., user queries, file uploads, real-time data) into the PoC, enabling users to interact meaningfully with the system.
* Project Clarification & Consultation: 
Allocate dedicated time for consultations, where instructors and peers can offer guidance, critique, and additional resources.
Learning Outcome:
* Demonstrate the ability to conceptualize, design, and implement a complete AI application from ideation through final prototype, leveraging all the modules (LLMs, prompt engineering, embeddings, RAG, Streamlit, etc.) covered in the course.
* Apply industry-standard methodologies (e.g., agile development, user-centric design) to structure the project’s lifecycle, from planning and requirements gathering to testing and deployment.
* Apply and build Python-based AI application, incorporating retrieval-augmented generation, and integrate multiple components - LLM chaining, embedding-based search, and web front-end.
